name: Elam
overview: Elam is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, known specifically as the son of Shashak. His identity is primarily established through this familial connection, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. He appears in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 8:24.
namesAndTitles: The name Elam means 'highland,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This name was not given by God but is recorded in Scripture to identify this individual distinctly within his lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Elam is explicitly identified as the son of Shashak, establishing his place within the Benjaminite genealogy. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Elam's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, which serve to preserve the heritage and continuity of God's chosen people. As the son of Shashak, his mention underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining the lineage through which His purposes are fulfilled. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, Elam contributes to the biblical record that traces God's providential care for His covenant community.
